Canada Navigates US Trade Tensions Amidst Shifting Economic Sentiment

Canadian Finance Minister Mark Carney has extended a gas tax holiday, a move occurring as the country faces escalating trade tensions with the United States. Analysts are raising Canadian dollar forecasts, anticipating that trade disputes will eventually subside. Some reports indicate that Canadian consumers are currently in a stronger position than their U.S. counterparts, with trade tensions fueling Canadian patriotism and leading some shoppers to shun American goods. Small businesses in Canada are reportedly rethinking their operational strategies due to the trade war. Meanwhile, a separate report highlights the case of international students facing ejection from Canada after protesting a work permit refusal.
